comparisons.peer_topic: Significant Customer Concentration in Revenue and Receivables
comparisons.peer_summary: One customer accounted for 18% and 21% of net accounts receivable as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, respectively, and represented 28%, 21%, and 20% of net revenue in fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022. This customer's revenue was included in the semiconductor solutions segment.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose concentration of trade receivables with specific single customers exceeding 10%, but they differ in magnitude and explicit credit risk assessment. Broadcom reported one customer at 18% (2024) and 21% (2023) of net accounts receivable, while AMD reported two customers at 24% and 16%. Unlike AMD, which explicitly states it does not believe these balances represent significant credit risk due to collection experience, Broadcom’s disclosure in this item does not include a similar explicit disclaimer regarding the credit risk associated with this high concentration, though it notes the revenue falls within its semiconductor solutions segment.

comparisons.comparison: Intel and AMD both address customer concentration in trade receivables and explicitly mitigate concerns by stating the balances do not represent significant credit risk. However, Intel reports a higher aggregate concentration among its top three customers (47% as of December 28, 2024) compared to AMD’s top two customers (24% and 16%). Intel attributes its low risk perception to cash flow forecasts and balance sheet analysis in addition to past collection experience, whereas AMD relies primarily on past collection experience and current credit quality reviews.
